variants.title: 5 Paise – 1957 (Naye Paise) Broad-Strike Error - Irregular Shape, Stretched Design - RARE & VALUABLE
variants.description: 1957 5 Naye Paise – Broad-Strike Error. Irregular shape, stretched design. First decimal transition year. RARE & VALUABLE. Coin struck outside collar, metal spread outside.

variants.title: 1984 25 Paise – Hyderabad Mint (STAR Mark) – Rare Key Date
variants.mint_mark: Hyderabad - STAR (★) - Star below 1984, between wreath bottom
variants.description:
25 Paisa – 1984 (Star Mark) – Hyderabad Mint. 

Key diagnostic: Must have a STAR mark (Hyderabad Mint) under the year. Check below 1984, center of wreath where both branches meet – small raised 5-pointed star must be present. 

Bombay mint has small dot • and Calcutta has no mark – those are common coins. Only Hyderabad Star is rare and valuable.

Material: Copper-Nickel, Weight: 2.83g, Size: 19mm.

This is original Hyderabad Star mint coin, natural worn condition, collector grade.

variants.title: 1980 25 Paise - Rural Women's Advancement (FAO) - Commemorative Coin - Bombay Mint
variants.description:
25 Paisa – 1980 (FAO) – "Rural Women's Advancement" Commemorative Issue.

Obverse: Ashoka Lion Capital with BHARAT / INDIA and 25 PAISE.

Reverse: Rural woman working with chaff cutter machine, village hut in background, legend "RURAL WOMEN'S ADVANCEMENT" in English and Hindi "Mahilaon Ke Liye Gramin Pragati" and year 1980 at bottom.

Mint: Bombay Mint – below year (Visible in image). Calcutta (No mark) and Hyderabad (Star) also exist for this year. All three mints can reach ₹100 to ₹1,500 in good condition.

This is a genuine 1980 FAO commemorative coin, highly collectible – first coin dedicated to Rural Women in India. Scalloped edge with 8 notches.

Material: Copper-Nickel, Weight: 2.83g, Diameter: 19mm.

Note: Value depends on mint and condition. UNC coins fetch premium.

variants.title: 1959 50 Naye Paise – Bombay Mint (DIAMOND Mark) – Early Decimal Key Date
variants.mint_mark: Bombay – DIAMOND (♦) – Below 1959, at wreath bottom center
variants.description:
50 Naye Paise – 1959 – Bombay Mint DIAMOND Mark.

Early decimal transition key date – First years of "Naye Paise" system (1957-1963). From 1964 onwards called "Paise" only, so "Naye" coins are special collector items.

Diagnostics: Must have DIAMOND mark ♦ below year 1959 at bottom center where wreath meets. Bombay Mint Diamond is the key identifier for this date.

Obverse: Ashoka Lion Capital with BHARAT / INDIA.
Reverse: 50 in large numerals, "NAYE PAISE" in Hindi, year 1959, laurel wreath border.

Material: Copper-Nickel, Weight: 5.00g, Diameter: 24mm, Shape: Round.

Condition: Needs to be crisp and clean for premium value. This coin in image is natural worn but clear Diamond mark visible – collectible grade.

Note: 1959 Bombay Diamond is much scarcer than Calcutta No Mark. True collector key date.

variants.title: 1988 50 Paise – Noida Mint DOT – Rare Key Date
variants.mint_mark: Noida – DOT ( • ) – Below Year 1988 – BIG DOT type Key diagnostic: Must have DOT below 1988
variants.description:
Fifty paise 1988 Noida mint dot – Rare variety.

Obverse: Ashoka Lion with INDIA / BHARAT.
Reverse: 50 PAISE, floral pattern border, year 1988 with Noida DOT mark below year (single dot with extra dot spacing – Noida diagnostic).

Noida mint started 1986, so early years 1986-88 are scarce. 1988 Noida dot is one of the most demanded in 50 paise series.

Material: Copper-Nickel, Weight: 4.90g.

Note: This is Noida mint – DOT must be visible below 1988 as in image. Bombay is small diamond/dot in different style. Noida DOT is larger and separated.

variants.title: 1986 50 Paise – Bombay Mint – Extremely Rare
variants.description:
Buy Extremely Rare 50 Paisa 1986 Bombay Mint.

Year: 1986 – First year of new floral design 50 Paise.
Mint: Bombay (Dot below year)
Material: Copper-Nickel.

Why Rare: 1986 Mumbai mintage was very low, and most went into circulation. Finding in good condition is extremely tough. Key date for 50 Paise collectors.

Obverse will be Lion capital with INDIA / BHARAT.

Condition as in image – collectible grade, clear year and mint mark visible.

variants.title: 1970 1 Rupee – Bombay Mint – The King of Republic Rupees – 10 Gram Nickel
variants.description: Must be the heavy 10-Gram Pure Nickel coin. This is the large, heavy, pure nickel issue which is highly valuable. Later 1970s rupees are lighter (6-gram)

variants.title: 1985 1 Rupee ERROR – No Mint Mark – Rare Trial / Error Issue
variants.mint_mark: Error – NO mint mark below year (Missing Mark)
variants.description:
Obverse: Ashoka Lion Capital with BHARAT / INDIA.
Reverse: 1 RUPEE 1985 with wheat stalks – BUT NO mint mark.

Condition: As per image – Year 1985 clearly visible with no mark below.

Note: This is a mint error, not a regular issue. One of the most famous error coins in Republic India series.

Value Range: ₹2,000 – ₹5,000 (Trial/Error Only) – UNC can go higher

Key Diagnostic: BLANK space below 1985 – No Dot, No Diamond, No Star.

variants.title: 1992 2 Rupees FAO – Land & Vital Resources – Proof Only – Never Issued to Public – Super Rare
variants.description: This coin was NEVER found in loose pocket change. It was only issued in the 1992 Certified Proof Set. If someone claims to have found it in circulation, it is FAKE. Only Proof Set coin is genuine and valuable. Design: FAO theme with Land & Vital Resources.

variants.title: 1998 2 Rupees Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das – Hyderabad STAR Mark – Rare Commemorative
